slides.title: Discover Marinduque
slides.subtitle: The heart-shaped island at the center of the Philippines: pristine beaches, centuries-old churches, hidden caves and waterfalls, and the legendary Moriones Festival.

slides.title: The Heart of the Philippines
slides.subtitle: Marinduque is a heart-shaped island province in the Mimaropa region, lying between Tayabas Bay and the Sibuyan Sea.

cards.title: Location
cards.desc: South of Luzon, between Tayabas Bay to the north and the Sibuyan Sea to the south.

cards.title: Geographic Center
cards.desc: The Luzon Datum of 1911 in Mogpog is the reference point for the country's maps and surveys.

cards.title: Six Municipalities
cards.desc: Boac (the capital), Mogpog, Gasan, Buenavista, Torrijos and Santa Cruz.

cards.title: Moriones Festival
cards.desc: A Holy Week tradition of masked Roman centurions, celebrated in Boac, Mogpog and Gasan.

cards.title: Islands & Beaches
cards.desc: White-sand islands, sandbars, dive sites and the long beaches of the mainland coast.

cards.title: Nature & Adventure
cards.desc: Mount Malindig, hot springs, waterfalls and some of the best-known caves in the region.

slides.title: Six Towns, One Island
slides.subtitle: Each municipality has its own character. Here is where this tour will take you.

cards.title: Boac
cards.desc: The heritage capital: hilltop cathedral, museum, ancestral houses and waterfalls.

cards.title: Mogpog
cards.desc: The gateway town: Luzon Datum, Paadjao Falls, caves and Moriones mask makers.

cards.title: Gasan
cards.desc: Tres Reyes Islands, butterfly gardens and the Gasang-Gasang Festival.

cards.title: Buenavista
cards.desc: Malindig country: the volcano, sulphur springs and Elephant Island.

cards.title: Torrijos
cards.desc: Poctoy White Beach, historic battlefields, caves and falls.

cards.title: Santa Cruz
cards.desc: The island-hopping hub: Maniwaya, Palad Sandbar, Ungab Rock and the great caves.

slides.title: The Heritage Capital
slides.subtitle: Nicknamed Montserrat de Marinduque, Boac is the provincial capital, a town of hilltop churches, ancestral houses and forest waterfalls.

slides.title: Boac Cathedral
slides.subtitle: Built in 1792, this hilltop church is regarded as one of the oldest in Marinduque, with a Filipino-Hispanic Gothic facade and an adobe bell tower.
slides.howToGet: A short tricycle ride from Boac town proper, followed by a climb up the hill to the church grounds.
slides.whatToDo: Admire the facade and bell tower, visit the venerated image of Our Lady of Biglang Awa, and take in views of the town and sea from the hilltop.
slides.tip: Dress modestly when visiting; the cathedral is an active place of worship.
slides.caption: Photo credit: Benedict Esber (Bengoeswhere), Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

slides.title: Marinduque Museum
slides.subtitle: The province's principal museum, housed in a heritage building, presents the island's history, culture and crafts.
slides.howToGet: Near the municipal hall area; reachable by tricycle from the Boac town proper.
slides.whatToDo: View historical exhibits, artifacts and traditional Moriones masks, and learn how the island's story connects to its festivals.
slides.tip: Pair it with the cathedral for a half-day heritage walk.

slides.title: Boac Heritage Town
slides.subtitle: Old streets and ancestral houses from the Spanish and American periods still stand below the cathedral hill.
slides.howToGet: Start from Boac's central plaza and public market and explore on foot.
slides.whatToDo: Stroll past ancestral homes, photograph period architecture, and stop at local cafes and pasalubong stores.
slides.tip: Early morning and late afternoon are the best times for walking and photography.

slides.title: Battle of Paye Monument
slides.subtitle: A historical marker commemorating the 1900 Battle of Paye, where Marinduque freedom fighters faced American forces during the Philippine-American War.
slides.howToGet: Take a jeepney or tricycle from the Boac town proper and ask locals for the marker.
slides.whatToDo: Learn about the island's role in the Philippine-American War and pay respects at the memorial.
slides.tip: Visit alongside the Battle of Pulang Lupa Shrine in Torrijos for the fuller story.

slides.title: Kabugsakan Falls
slides.subtitle: A cascade of roughly 40 feet tucked in the forested interior of Boac, with a cool natural pool at its base.
slides.howToGet: Travel by tricycle or habal-habal to the trailhead, then continue on foot with a local guide.
slides.whatToDo: Swim in the pool, enjoy a picnic by the water, and photograph the falls surrounded by greenery.
slides.tip: Avoid visiting during or right after heavy rain; trails and rocks become slippery.

slides.title: Busay & Lambingan Falls
slides.subtitle: Two more of Boac's refreshing waterfalls, set deep in the island's forested uplands.
slides.howToGet: Arrange a guide through the municipal tourism office or a local resort; access roads can be rough.
slides.whatToDo: Go waterfall-hopping, swim in the cool pools and enjoy a day in the hills.
slides.tip: Bring water shoes, a dry bag and plenty of drinking water.

slides.title: Mainit Hot Springs
slides.subtitle: Free-flowing springs of warm, therapeutic water, a long-time favorite of Marinduquenos and the main draw of Barangay Mainit.
slides.howToGet: Take a tricycle or habal-habal from Boac town proper to Barangay Mainit.
slides.whatToDo: Soak in the warm water and relax after a day of touring.
slides.tip: Go in the morning or evening when the air is cooler.

slides.title: Duyay Cave
slides.subtitle: A large, dark cave system filled with stalactites. Few visitors have explored its full length, which is said to run toward Tapuyan in Gasan.
slides.howToGet: Ask the tourism office for a guide, then travel by road and on foot.
slides.whatToDo: Explore the chambers and tunnels with a guide.
slides.tip: Bring a headlamp, spare batteries and sturdy shoes.

slides.title: Balagasan Caves
slides.subtitle: Two separate caves about 100 meters apart. The larger one can be explored using rappel ropes.
slides.howToGet: Arrange a guide and ropes through the municipal tourism office.
slides.whatToDo: Try cave rappelling and look for rock formations.
slides.tip: Only attempt the rappel with an experienced guide.

slides.title: Ginaras Falls
slides.subtitle: A 100-meter fall with six smaller falls beside it, set in the mountains of Barangay Duyay.
slides.howToGet: Reach Duyay by road, then trek on foot with a local guide.
slides.whatToDo: Trek to the falls and swim in the cool pools.
slides.tip: Wear grippy footwear; the trail can be slippery.

slides.title: Amoingon Coastal Reef
slides.subtitle: A coastal area where marine life is visible 10 to 15 meters from the beachfront: butterflyfish, clownfish, lionfish and angelfish.
slides.howToGet: Travel by tricycle or jeepney from Boac town proper.
slides.whatToDo: Snorkel the shallow reef right off the shore.
slides.tip: Do not touch or stand on the coral.

slides.title: Biglang-Awa Shrine & Marinduque Trade House
slides.subtitle: The shrine houses the patroness of the province, while the nearby trade house showcases products by Marinduque makers.
slides.howToGet: Both are reachable by tricycle from the town center.
slides.whatToDo: Visit the shrine, then browse local products for pasalubong.
slides.tip: Check opening hours with the tourism office first.

slides.title: Gateway to the Heart
slides.subtitle: Mogpog welcomes most visitors at Balanacan Port. It is also known as the Home of the Original Moriones and holds the geodetic center of the Philippines.

slides.title: Luzon Datum of 1911
slides.subtitle: A stone marker atop Mataas na Bundok that serves as the primary geodetic reference point for Philippine maps and surveys, also known as Station Balanacan.
slides.howToGet: Go by tricycle or jeepney to the foot of Mataas na Bundok, then climb the stairway of several hundred steps to the hilltop.
slides.whatToDo: Stand at the marker that anchors Philippine mapping, enjoy views of the surrounding coast and sea, and take a commemorative photo.
slides.tip: Climb in the morning to avoid the midday heat.

slides.title: Paadjao Falls
slides.subtitle: Cascading about 100 feet into a natural pool, Paadjao is one of Mogpog's most beloved nature spots.
slides.howToGet: Travel from Mogpog town proper to Barangay Bocboc, then continue on a short walk to the falls.
slides.whatToDo: Swim in the pool, look for the natural rock tubs downstream, and enjoy a picnic or camping.
slides.tip: A good choice for families; go on a dry day for the safest footing.

slides.title: Balanacan Port & Cove
slides.subtitle: The island's main sea gateway, with a large image of Our Lady of Biglang Awa greeting travelers at the shore.
slides.howToGet: Ferries from Dalahican Port in Lucena arrive here; tricycles and jeepneys wait at the port.
slides.whatToDo: Watch ferries come and go, photograph the shoreline and the Marian statue, and enjoy the cove at sunset.
slides.tip: Allow time here when arriving or leaving; it's a pleasant first and last stop.

slides.title: Bintakay Cave
slides.subtitle: A cave of both natural and historical interest, said to have served as a battle site during the revolution.
slides.howToGet: Arrange a local guide through the municipal tourism office and travel to the site by tricycle or habal-habal.
slides.whatToDo: Explore the cave with a guide, learn its wartime history and observe the rock formations.
slides.tip: Bring a flashlight or headlamp and wear sturdy shoes.

slides.title: Tarug Caves
slides.subtitle: Another of Mogpog's cave attractions for travelers who enjoy spelunking away from the crowds.
slides.howToGet: Coordinate with the municipal tourism office or a local guide; access is by road, then a short walk.
slides.whatToDo: Take a guided walk through the chambers and look for stalactites and other cave formations.
slides.tip: Never enter caves without a local guide.

slides.title: Moriones Mask Makers
slides.subtitle: Mogpog calls itself the Home of the Original Moriones, and local artisans still carve and paint the festival's famous masks.
slides.howToGet: Ask at the municipal hall or tourism office to be directed to the mask makers.
slides.whatToDo: Watch masks and helmets being crafted, learn their meaning, and bring one home as a souvenir.
slides.tip: Visit before Holy Week to see workshops at their busiest.
slides.caption: Photo credit: Wikimedia Commons, file "Moriones of Marinduque.jpg" (license needs verification before use).

slides.title: Natangco Islet
slides.subtitle: An eight-hectare islet off Balanacan with a short stretch of white sand and waters rich in coral and marine life.
slides.howToGet: Hire a boat from Balanacan.
slides.whatToDo: Dive, snorkel or picnic on the sand.
slides.tip: Bring your own water and food; there are no facilities.

slides.title: Islands & Butterflies
slides.subtitle: Gasan is the island's southern gateway, home to the Tres Reyes Islands, butterfly gardens and the lively Gasang-Gasang Festival.

slides.title: Tres Reyes Islands
slides.subtitle: Three islets off the coast, Gaspar, Melchor and Baltazar, named for the Three Kings. Gaspar has a small white-sand beach, Melchor is cliff-edged, and Baltazar is a prized dive site.
slides.howToGet: Hire a motorized boat from the Gasan shoreline or arrange island hopping through a mainland resort.
slides.whatToDo: Snorkel and dive among coral gardens, relax on Gaspar's beach and photograph the rock formations.
slides.tip: Check sea conditions with boatmen before departing.

slides.title: Gasan Nature & Butterfly Park
slides.subtitle: A garden attraction that shows visitors Marinduque's butterfly culture and local biodiversity.
slides.howToGet: A short jeepney or tricycle ride from the town proper.
slides.whatToDo: Walk through the gardens, see butterflies at different life stages, and learn about local breeding.
slides.tip: Best visited in the morning when butterflies are most active.

slides.title: Talao Cave
slides.subtitle: A cave in Gasan that adds an underground adventure to the town's coastal and garden attractions.
slides.howToGet: Hire a guide through the local tourism office; reach the site by road, then on foot.
slides.whatToDo: Explore the cave chambers and spot natural formations with your guide.
slides.tip: Bring a headlamp and wear shoes with good grip.

slides.title: Gasan Town & Gasang-Gasang Festival
slides.subtitle: Gasan celebrates with street dancing at the Gasang-Gasang Festival and joins the island's Moriones Holy Week rites.
slides.howToGet: A short jeepney ride south of Boac along the coastal road.
slides.whatToDo: Shop for butterfly-themed crafts, sample Marinduque's famous arrowroot cookies (uraro) and catch a festival if you time your visit.
slides.tip: Check the provincial tourism office for the latest festival dates.

slides.title: Malindig Country
slides.subtitle: Buenavista lies in the shadow of Mount Malindig, with healing waters, rolling hills and a famous island resort just offshore.

slides.title: Mount Malindig
slides.subtitle: At 1,157 meters, Marinduque's highest peak is a potentially active volcano shared by Buenavista and Torrijos, with an easy-to-moderate climb.
slides.howToGet: Trailheads are reached by tricycle or habal-habal from Buenavista or Torrijos; hire a local guide.
slides.whatToDo: Hike through grassland, farmland and mossy forest. Viewpoints along the trail look out on Tres Reyes, Elephant Island, Mindoro and Verde Island.
slides.tip: Start early; clouds often cover the summit by midday.

slides.title: Malbog Sulphur Spring
slides.subtitle: Natural sulphur pools at the foot of Mount Malindig, believed by locals to have therapeutic properties.
slides.howToGet: Take a tricycle or jeepney from Buenavista town proper.
slides.whatToDo: Soak in warm, mineral-rich waters after a day of hiking or travel. A nearby resort also offers hot spring pools.
slides.tip: Sulphur's smell can cling to clothes; bring a change.

slides.title: Elephant Island & Bellarocca
slides.subtitle: Named for its elephant-like shape, this islet off Barangay Lipata is home to the Bellarocca Island Resort and Spa and a sheltered beach.
slides.howToGet: A short boat transfer from the mainland jetty; arrange access through the resort.
slides.whatToDo: Enjoy sweeping sea views, swim or snorkel, and photograph the island against Malindig's backdrop.
slides.tip: Access is typically arranged through the resort; check ahead.

slides.title: Haynon Hills
slides.subtitle: Rolling grassy hills that locals nickname the Chocolate Hills of Buenavista, with wide landscape views.
slides.howToGet: Ask locals or the tourism office for current directions; reachable by motorcycle or tricycle.
slides.whatToDo: Walk the hilltops, enjoy sunset views and photograph the countryside.
slides.tip: Bring sun protection; there is little shade on the hills.

slides.title: Coastlines & Battlefields
slides.subtitle: Torrijos is the island's southeastern town, with its best-known white-sand beach, a historic battle shrine and forest caves and falls.

slides.title: Poctoy White Beach
slides.subtitle: A kilometer-long stretch of fine white sand facing the Sibuyan Sea, with Mount Malindig rising behind it.
slides.howToGet: Take a jeepney or bus from Boac or Santa Cruz to Torrijos, then a tricycle to the beach.
slides.whatToDo: Swim, snorkel, rent a cottage, camp under the stars and try fresh grilled seafood.
slides.tip: A small municipal entrance fee may apply.

slides.title: Battle of Pulang Lupa Shrine
slides.subtitle: A hilltop park marking the September 1900 battle in which Marinduque forces led by Col. Maximo Abad defeated an American column.
slides.howToGet: Take a jeepney or tricycle from Torrijos town proper and ride uphill to the shrine.
slides.whatToDo: Read the markers, walk the grounds and appreciate the countryside views from the shrine.
slides.tip: Combine it with Poctoy for a day of history and beach time.

slides.title: Ka Amon Cave
slides.subtitle: A cave in Torrijos for visitors who want to try spelunking in a less-visited part of the island.
slides.howToGet: Arrange a local guide through the municipal tourism office.
slides.whatToDo: Explore the chamber with your guide and observe the formations.
slides.tip: Wear sturdy shoes and carry a light source.

slides.title: Basud Falls
slides.subtitle: One of Torrijos's inland waterfalls, a quiet spot for a refreshing dip.
slides.howToGet: Travel by tricycle or habal-habal to the trailhead, then walk with a guide.
slides.whatToDo: Swim in the pool, rest in the shade and enjoy the forest soundscape.
slides.tip: Check weather first; river levels rise quickly in heavy rain.

slides.title: Tabag Falls
slides.subtitle: Another of Torrijos's cascades, set in the forested hills inland from the coast.
slides.howToGet: Hire a local guide at the barangay or through the tourism office.
slides.whatToDo: Take a cooling swim, relax and enjoy a short nature trek.
slides.tip: Pack out all your trash to keep the falls pristine.

slides.title: Costa Celina
slides.subtitle: A dive spot flanked by cliffs, with an undersea wall about 40 meters from shore that is rich in marine plants and animals.
slides.howToGet: Travel by road from Torrijos town proper to Sitio Talisay.
slides.whatToDo: Dive or snorkel along the undersea wall.
slides.tip: Check sea conditions and book a local dive guide.

slides.title: The Island-Hopping Gateway
slides.subtitle: Santa Cruz is Marinduque's largest municipality, with powder-white islands and sandbars offshore and some of the island's biggest caves inland.

slides.title: Maniwaya Island
slides.subtitle: A long stretch of powdery white sand and turquoise water, lined with cottages and coconut palms and facing the mainland mountains.
slides.location: Off the coast of Santa Cruz
slides.howToGet: Take a motorized outrigger boat from Buyabod Port; resorts on the island can arrange transfers.
slides.whatToDo: Swim, kayak, paddleboard, camp on the sand and use the island as a base for nearby attractions.
slides.tip: Book accommodations and boat transfers in advance during holidays.

slides.title: Palad Sandbar
slides.subtitle: A long white sandbar near Maniwaya that seems to float on the sea when the tide is right.
slides.howToGet: Ask your Maniwaya resort or boatmen to take you; trips are short.
slides.whatToDo: Wade in the shallows, photograph the sandbar and enjoy the open sea views.
slides.tip: Check tides and give other visitors space for photos.

slides.title: Mongpong Island & Ungab Rock
slides.subtitle: The farthest of the offshore islands, with a long white beach of crushed coral and the arching Ungab Rock formation about 100 feet high.
slides.location: Off the coast of Santa Cruz
slides.howToGet: Arrange a boat from Buyabod Port or a Maniwaya resort.
slides.whatToDo: Photograph the Ungab Rock arch, swim along the east beach and dive at the island's northern sites.
slides.tip: Seas can be rough; travel with experienced boatmen.

slides.title: Bathala Caves
slides.subtitle: A complex of seven caves, four of which are open to visitors: Church Cave, Secret Cave, Python Cave and Cemetery Cave.
slides.howToGet: Hire a habal-habal and a local guide from Santa Cruz town proper.
slides.whatToDo: Walk through chambers with stalactites and stalagmites, see resident bats and learn the caves' folklore.
slides.tip: Bring a headlamp; the caves are dark and uneven.

slides.title: Bagumbungan Cave
slides.subtitle: A cave of about 1.9 kilometers with small waterfalls and an underground stream, popular with adventurous spelunkers.
slides.howToGet: Arrange a local guide and a ride from Santa Cruz town proper.
slides.whatToDo: Climb, duck and wade through chambers of stalactites and flowstone. Two routes are available: a halfway turn-back or the full traverse.
slides.tip: Moderate fitness is required; wear shoes that can get wet.

slides.title: Kawa-Kawa Falls
slides.subtitle: A set of cascades with several kettle-like wading pools, a favorite for a quick, relaxed swim.
slides.howToGet: A short ride from Santa Cruz town proper followed by an easy walk.
slides.whatToDo: Wade through the pools, picnic by the water and take photos of the cascades.
slides.tip: Bring a dry bag and waterproof camera.

slides.title: Carmen Eco-Adventure Park
slides.subtitle: An outdoor park that adds activities and nature experiences to the Santa Cruz itinerary.
slides.howToGet: Reach by tricycle or habal-habal from Santa Cruz town proper; check opening times first.
slides.whatToDo: Enjoy the park's outdoor activities and the greenery.
slides.tip: Confirm activities and rates with the park before visiting.

slides.title: Baluarte de Santa Cruz
slides.subtitle: A Spanish-colonial defensive structure that reminds visitors of the island's coastal past.
slides.howToGet: Ask locals or the tourism office for directions from the town proper.
slides.whatToDo: See the old stonework, learn about the town's history and take photographs.
slides.tip: Wear comfortable shoes; the ground can be uneven.

slides.title: Polo Island
slides.subtitle: An islet about 35 minutes by boat from the Santa Cruz pier, with a white-sand beach and low sandy cliffs along its coast.
slides.location: Off the coast of Santa Cruz
slides.howToGet: Hire a boat at the Santa Cruz pier.
slides.whatToDo: Swim, picnic and camp on the beach.
slides.tip: Bring drinking water and camping gear.

slides.title: Salomague Island
slides.subtitle: A privately owned island with a half-kilometer white beach of crushed coral and a good dive site to its northeast.
slides.location: Off the coast of Santa Cruz
slides.howToGet: Hire a boat from Santa Cruz.
slides.whatToDo: Dive off the northeast side of the islet.
slides.tip: Secure permission before landing; the island is private.

slides.title: Santa Cruz Church
slides.subtitle: Built in 1714 and renovated in later years, its tower still keeps its original solidity.
slides.howToGet: A short tricycle ride within Santa Cruz town proper.
slides.whatToDo: Admire the old tower and the church grounds.
slides.tip: Dress modestly; it is an active place of worship.

slides.title: Festivals & Traditions
slides.subtitle: Marinduque's calendar is full of colorful celebrations rooted in faith and community.

cards.title: Moriones Festival
cards.desc: Holy Week reenactment of the story of Longinus, with masked and costumed centurions in Boac, Mogpog and Gasan.

cards.title: Putong
cards.desc: A traditional welcome ceremony with songs, prayers and dances, offered to honored guests.

cards.title: Kangga Festival
cards.desc: Mogpog's cultural celebration, featuring decorated carts and street processions.

cards.title: Bila-Bila Festival
cards.desc: Boac's festival highlighting the town's heritage and community spirit.

cards.title: Gasang-Gasang Festival
cards.desc: Gasan's lively street dancing and pageantry.

cards.title: Immaculate Conception Fiesta
cards.desc: Boac's town fiesta falls on the feast of the Immaculate Conception on December 8.

slides.title: Food & Pasalubong
slides.subtitle: Bring home a taste, or a piece, of the island.

cards.title: Uraro (Arrowroot) Cookies
cards.desc: Marinduque's most famous pasalubong: light, crumbly cookies made from arrowroot.

cards.title: Moriones Masks
cards.desc: Hand-carved and painted masks and helmets, made by local artisans.

cards.title: Fresh Seafood
cards.desc: Grilled fish and shellfish at beachfront cottages, especially along the coast.

cards.title: Local Crafts
cards.desc: Woven goods, framed souvenirs and handmade keepsakes from town markets.

slides.title: Getting There & Around
slides.subtitle: Marinduque is reached by sea from Lucena, Quezon, with other options depending on schedules.

cards.title: By Ferry
cards.desc: Ferries from Dalahican Port in Lucena arrive at Balanacan (Mogpog), Cawit (Boac) and Buyabod (Santa Cruz).

cards.title: By Bus and Ferry
cards.desc: Bus lines from Metro Manila connect with the ferry at Lucena and continue on the island.

cards.title: By Air
cards.desc: Marinduque Airport is in Gasan. Flight availability changes, so check current schedules.

cards.title: Getting Around
cards.desc: Jeepneys, tricycles and habal-habal link the towns; motorcycles can be rented for flexibility.

slides.title: Travel Tips
slides.subtitle: A few notes to make your visit smoother and more responsible.

cards.title: Time Your Visit
cards.desc: Holy Week is Moriones season. Book transport and lodging well ahead.

cards.title: Dry Weather for the Sea
cards.desc: Calmer, drier months are best for island hopping and for waterfall and cave trips.

cards.title: Use Local Guides
cards.desc: Caves, falls and Malindig are best done with a guide who knows the terrain.

cards.title: Carry Cash
cards.desc: Many rural attractions and boatmen accept cash only. Bring enough with you.

cards.title: Stay Safe
cards.desc: Check weather and sea conditions, and avoid caves and rivers after heavy rain.

cards.title: Travel Responsibly
cards.desc: Take your trash with you, respect wildlife and support community-run services.
